subject: Re: Emapex renewal — commit-anchored bridging proposal
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@emapex.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal discussion — proposal framework

Hi Sophie — great talking yesterday. Summary and next steps below.

Goal: Keep Emapex on a predictable per-token effective price as you scale into Q1, while giving you headroom for a mid-year capacity surge.

Proposal (high level):
- 12-month renewal (Jan 1–Dec 31 2027) with a commit anchor at 60M tokens/month (baseline).
- Price hold for first 6 months at current list minus 18% (applied to generation tokens) in exchange for the commit anchor.
- Temporary bridging credits: 100k token credits applied in Q1 for migration/initial burst.
- Phased overage: burst pool available at a capped rate (20% uplift over commit price) until commit true-up at month 7.

Why this helps you: predictable unit economics for planning, short-term credits to cover migration and spike risk, and a clear path for true-up or capacity increase with minimal disruption.

Can you confirm procurement timing and whether Emapex needs a PO vs DocuSign signature? I can draft a clean term sheet and loop in finance/ops.

Attachments: I will send a draft term sheet and a simple forecast sheet once you confirm PO/DocuSign preference.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@emapex.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — proposal framework

Alex — thanks for the summary. Procurement notes below.

- We like the idea of a 12-month anchor but need a 90-day pricing rollback clause if our monthly consumption falls below 40% of the anchor three months running. Can you accommodate?
- PO preferred for renewals > $50k/month; DocuSign is acceptable if you can provide an invoice-ready term sheet.
- Can the bridging credits be applied to inference generation only? (We separate embedding and generation budgets).

Also, need a high-level replacement/rollback path if new model variants materially change unit cost effectiveness mid-term. Procurement wants a mechanism to re-open economics vs a fixed-locked price.

I'll loop procurement on signature preference after I see the draft.

— Sophie
Sophie Lang
Head of Procurement, Emapex
sophie.lang@emapex.com | +1 617-555-0134

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@emapex.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement Team <procure@emapex.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — proposal framework

Sophie — appreciate the specifics, good asks. Quick answers and tweaks we can include in the term sheet: 

- 90-day rollback clause: yes — we can include a consumption floor trigger and a 90-day review window. If usage stays below 40% of anchor for three consecutive months, pricing will be re-negotiated (we'll propose a tiered step-down rather than an immediate increase).
- Bridging credits: can be scoped to generation tokens only, we'll call this out explicitly.
- Model variant clause: propose an "economics review" window at month 6 and on material model replacements ( >15% change in per-token cost). The review gives both parties 30 days to agree on adjustments or elect a migration path to newer variants with support credits.

Internal note: looping Laura for onboarding commitments and Karthik for approval on discount depth and credit sizing.

I will attach a draft term sheet (simple = price table, credits, triggers, signature block) by EOD Monday. Which sign path do you prefer — I can create a PO-ready PDF or a DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — proposal framework (internal)

Alex / Laura — quick internal alignment before we finalize the draft.

Considerations:
- 18% off list for first 6 months is acceptable if commit anchor and true-up process are clear. Approve on my side pending finance confirmation of effective ARR/ACV.
- Bridging credits: 100k generation tokens ok; can be billed as a credit line item so invoicing matches PO.
- Rollback trigger: prefer tiered step-down that phases price change over 2 months to avoid sudden margin shock.
- Model variant economics review: OK but include a cap on downside movement (max increase of 8% without a separate exec sign-off).

I will ask Finance to pre-clear the discount in the CRM approval queue. Laura, can you confirm onboarding SLA commitments and whether we can offer a 2-week migration support credit during the model migration window?

Karthik
Head of Sales — East, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@emapex.com>, Procurement Team <procure@emapex.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:42:00-08:00
Subject: Final: Emapex term sheet and next steps (attached)

Sophie / Procurement — attaching the draft term sheet and a short forecast workbook. Key points called out in the doc:

- 12-month commit anchor: 60M tokens/month baseline.
- Price hold: first 6 months at current rate less 18% (generation tokens only).
- Bridging credits: 100k generation-only credits, itemized on invoice Q1.
- Overage: capped burst pool at +20% rate, available until month 7 true-up.
- Consumption floor & rollback: if usage <40% anchor for 3 consecutive months, tiered step-down applied over 60 days; 90-day review rights preserved.
- Model economics review: month 6 and on material model substitution (>15% per-token cost change). Downside cap of 8% without exec sign-off.

Requested next steps:
1) Confirm sign route (PO vs DocuSign) — Sophie, you mentioned PO preferred; we'll produce a PO-ready invoice line.
2) If PO: please share PO number and billing contact. If DocuSign: we'll send envelope and routing.
3) Signatures target: by Nov 12 to preserve price hold for Jan 1 start.

Attachments: emapex_renewal_term_sheet_20261102.pdf (term sheet), usage-forecast_emapex_Q4-2026.xlsx (forecast). Also linking the HubSpot deal above.

If you want small phrasing tweaks before sharing with legal/procurement, tell me and I'll update.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: emapex_renewal_term_sheet_20261102.pdf (PDF, 3 pages), usage-forecast_emapex_Q4-2026.xlsx (XLSX, 1 sheet)
